_provenance.source: OpenStreetMap Overpass API, relation 4829792 "Enchantments Traverse" (operator: Okanogan-Wenatchee National Forest, route=hiking), stitched from its 25 member ways by exact shared OSM node id, with 4 small digitization gaps (2.6-11.3 m) bridged by nearest-endpoint matching. Retrieved 2026-08-21. Endpoints independently confirmed against named USFS trailhead nodes: "Stuart Lake Trailhead" (OSM node 11298873822) and "Snow Lakes Trailhead" (OSM node 1666358934, highway=trailhead, operator=US Forest Service).
_provenance.note: There is no physical km-marker-post system on this trail (unlike the SCT). routeKm and measuredKm are therefore the SAME computed distance-along-this-line for every vertex — not two independent systems. See src/features/track/trailLength.ts and docs/PORT-DECISIONS.md (P1) for why. Elevation is sampled from a public DEM (SRTM 30 m via opentopodata), fetched 2026-08-23 — every vertex filled, none interpolated. A DEM is not a survey; heights carry the model's own error, larger on steep terrain like Aasgard.

quality.measuredKmMeaning: distance along this OSM-derived line, computed by great-circle summation between consecutive vertices — the only distance figure this dataset has, since there is no separate marker-post system to compare it against.
quality.note: This line is OSM crowd-sourced geometry, not a surveyed or GPS-recorded track. AllTrails independently lists 18.5–19.1 mi (29.8–30.7 km) for the same route (research/osm-permit-zones adjacent screenshots, 2026-08-21) — about 3–6% longer than this line's 28.87 km. Per the SCT lesson this app is built around, a map line usually reads SHORT relative to true walking distance, so treat 28.87 km as a floor, not a ceiling, until a GPS-recorded thru-hike replaces it.

evidence.what: Stuart Lake Trailhead -> Snow Lakes Trailhead, whole route
evidence.source: This dataset (OSM relation 4829792) measures 28.87 km. AllTrails' own listing gives three slightly different figures for the same route across its own screens — 19.1 mi (listing header), 18.51 mi (route builder), 18.5 mi (segment row) — i.e. 29.8–30.7 km. Neither AllTrails number is copied here: hard rule 1 forbids scaling a measured line to match a secondary source.

elevation.note: Sampled from a public DEM (SRTM 30 m via opentopodata), fetched 2026-08-23 — every vertex filled, none interpolated. Not a survey; heights carry the model’s own error, larger on steep terrain like Aasgard Pass. No cumulative climb total is published: the traced line reads SHORT and DEM elevation deltas are noisy, so summing them into a gain figure would be guesswork in both directions. Read the profile for the shape of a day, not the exact metre.
